run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:55:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend alert reflects frontend's own failed requests: frontend recorded 500s on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout caused by failures of two downstream dependencies - its gRPC calls to AdService/GetAds returned gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE with 'connect: connection refused' to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080, and its CheckoutService/PlaceOrder calls returned gRPC 13 INTERNAL because checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls were refused at the payment Service ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080. Frontend errors were zero for 5-minute windows ending 00:35:25-00:50:25, non-zero from the window ending 00:55:25 (the alert start), peaked in the window ending 01:00:25 and had stopped rising by 01:03:31 (cumulative GetAds error-span count flat at 802 afterwards). Exactly the two services whose calls were refused - the ad and payment Deployments - were rolled out at 2026-11-18T00:53:51Z via 'kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt' with an otherwise identical pod template (same image, env, resources); the old pods ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb were deleted at 00:53:54/00:53:55 and the new pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and are listed as ready endpoints. The only fault-injection configuration found in the cluster is ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, which is mounted by the flagd Deployment and has two enabled flags naming exactly those two services: adFailure (defaultVariant 'on', 'Fail ad service') and paymentFailure (defaultVariant '100%', 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'); the ad service resolves boolean flags through flagd and the payment service resolves float flags through flagd. No NetworkPolicy objects exist, no resource quota was found, and no OOM/eviction/restart marks appear on the ad or payment pods. The conclusion is partial because the declared fault behaviour itself was not observed at the ad/payment servers (their own error-span counts are 0 for payment and a single flagd EventStream error for ad, and the read ad logs show normal ad serving), the failures were transport-level connection refusals, and change history is not integrated, so the time the flag values were set and who/what triggered the 00:53:51 rollout restart remain unknown.

claims.text: Frontend error spans in the 4566s window ending 2026-11-18T01:11:31Z: GET 387.15, GET /api/data 387.15, executing api route (pages) /api/data 387.15, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 387.15, POST 42.68, POST /api/checkout 42.68, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 42.68, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.68, tcp.connect 15.24 (increase of trace span counts, not unique requests).

In 900s windows ending 00:40:25, 00:55:25 and 01:10:25 the dominant frontend error operation is grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (0, 12.41, 315.62), with grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder far smaller (0, 9.31, 2.11) and GET /api/data tracking GetAds exactly.

The cumulative count of frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error spans is flat at 421 from 00:32:31 to 00:55:31, rises to 433 at 00:56:31 and to 802 by 01:03:31, and stays 802 through the last sample at 01:09:31.

Exact error text on frontend client spans: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error span carries '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080'; frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carries '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card ... rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'; checkout's own oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with 'connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

Service ad is ClusterIP 100.65.180.246 port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad; Service payment is ClusterIP 100.70.188.60 port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment - the two addresses named in the connection-refused errors.

At query time the ad and payment Endpoints objects each have one ready address pointing at the new pods: ad -> ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (100.96.4.142:8080), payment -> payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (100.96.4.221:8080); this is the state when the query ran, not necessarily during the incident.

Events in otel-demo at 00:53:51-00:53:55 record Deployment/ad and Deployment/payment ScalingReplicaSet (new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 scaled 0->1, old ReplicaSets scaled 1->0), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Created/Started for ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84, and Pod Killing plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete for ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb.

The new ad and payment ReplicaSet pod templates are identical to the old ones (same images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-payment, same env, same resource requests/limits) except for the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:53:51Z; both ReplicaSets are owned by Deployments ad and payment.

Pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (image sha256:c9d4f943...) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (sha256:342c8ce5...) are Running, Ready since 00:53:54/00:53:55, with restartCount 0 and empty lastState (no terminated previous instance); owner chain is pod -> ReplicaSet (pod-template-hash 6cb57f76d / 9c8ffb665) -> Deployment ad / payment.
All 21 otel-demo Deployments, including ad, payment, frontend, checkout and flagd, report availableReplicas=1, readyReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1 with Available=True at query time.
ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config contains flag adFailure with defaultVariant 'on', description 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED, variants off=false / on=true.

The same ConfigMap contains flag paymentFailure with defaultVariant '100%', description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED, numeric variants (10%,25%,50%,75%,90%,100% = 0.1..1, off=0); its other flags (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, paymentUnreachable) have defaultVariant 'off'.

Deployment flagd mounts ConfigMap flagd-config as volume config-ro and its init-config container copies it into config-rw used by the flagd container at /etc/flagd, so flagd-config is the flag source served to the demo services.

The ad service has spans for flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (boolean flags), and the payment service has spans for grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat (a float/percentage flag), confirming both services evaluate flags through flagd.

Ad pod logs from the current container show it serving ad traffic normally ('Targeted ad request received for [...]', 'Non-targeted ad request received') between 01:02:47Z and 01:03:17Z with no error/fail/warn lines in the lines read.
A cluster-wide query returned no NetworkPolicy objects (empty list) and no ResourceQuota objects.

Ad-service span activity per 120s window is 108 at 00:55:31 and then 0 for windows ending 00:57:31, 00:59:31, 01:01:31 and 01:03:31, returning to 128 at 01:05:31, while frontend span activity stayed at ~3500-4300 per window throughout.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 started 2026-11-18T00:20:08Z with restartCount 0 and the checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-q5fkd started 00:20:08Z with restartCount 0, so neither caller was restarted around 00:53:51.

Flagd client-stream errors are small and largely outside the error burst: over the whole 4566s window ad has 1.02 error spans (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream), fraud-detection 3.05 and recommendation 4.06 (EventStream), and ad's single EventStream error falls in the window ending 00:50:25, before the frontend error onset.

Checkout's own error spans over the 4566s window are oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 34.83 and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 34.83 (all errors of that service); no other service except frontend (387/42.7), ad (1.02 flagd EventStream), fraud-detection (3.05) and recommendation (4.06) shows error spans in that window.

The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the origin of the injected fault: its enabled flags adFailure='on' ('Fail ad service') and paymentFailure='100%' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') name exactly the two dependencies whose calls failed, and it is the only fault-injection configuration in the cluster; the 00:53:51 restart of the ad and payment Deployments (unchanged pod template) and the subsequent frontend/checkout error burst would then be mechanism and consequence.

A second candidate cause is the 2026-11-18T00:53:51Z rollout restart of the ad and payment Deployments itself: it is one minute before the frontend error burst and precisely targets the two refused services, so transient stale endpoints/connections after the pod replacement could produce 'connection refused' while the replacement pods are Ready; the restart alone does not explain an ~8 minute refusal period and its trigger is unknown.

Server-side telemetry does not show the declared application-level faults: over the whole window payment records 0 error spans and ad records only 1.02 flagd EventStream error spans (no GetAds error spans), while the read ad container logs show normal ad serving at 01:02-01:03 - the observed failures are transport-level connection refusals recorded on the callers' client spans.

The ad service reported zero spans in the 120s windows ending 00:57:31-01:03:31, which would suggest it received no traffic then, yet its container logs show ad requests at 01:02:47-01:03:17; the two signals conflict, so the ad-side traffic gap is not reliable evidence of what ad experienced.

Rejected: resource exhaustion, OOMKilled or eviction on ad/payment. Both pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState/termination state, and no Pod Evicted/Failed/OOM events appear in the otel-demo event set (only Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing and ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete).
Rejected: a NetworkPolicy blocking frontend->ad or checkout->payment. A cluster-wide query returned no NetworkPolicy objects at all.

Rejected as the current problem: ad/payment Service selector or endpoint misconfiguration. Service selectors (opentelemetry.io/name=ad and =payment) match the running pods' labels and each Service has one ready endpoint at port 8080; this is the state at query time only, so it cannot rule out a transient endpoint gap at 00:54-01:03.

Rejected: the flagd pod itself being down. Deployment flagd reports 1/1 available with Available=True and the flagd pod started 00:21:48Z with restartCount 0, and flagd stream errors in the demo services are few and mostly outside the error burst (ad's single EventStream error precedes it).

Verify the effective flag values through flagd (flagd-ui/flagd service) and change history for ConfigMap flagd-config, and confirm whether adFailure/paymentFailure were deliberately enabled before treating the fault as confirmed; compare with the ad/payment server-side gRPC error metrics once available.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so it is unknown when flagd-config's adFailure and paymentFailure values were set to 'on'/'100%', and who or what issued the 00:53:51Z rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment (only the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation is visible).

The declared fault behaviour itself was not observed: neither ad nor payment produced application-level error spans or error log lines in the sampled data, and the failures recorded were transport-level 'connection refused' at the Service ClusterIPs, so the causal mechanism from the flag values to the refusals is unverified.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_*) are not present in this Prometheus (a selector on {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing), so historical pod/displacement readiness, per-deployment replica counts and image digests over time could not be checked; Kubernetes objects only show the state at query time.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not found in Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with that name returned no data), so the alert expression and the reported value 2.5777 could not be reproduced; the corresponding alert is not verifiable from this source.

Application logs could not be read for frontend (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data for frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5) nor for flagd (no_data for flagd-56d9c6c679-xwgx9), so the frontend-side error log text and flagd-side flag-serving logs are unknown.

The ad service span series shows zero spans for windows ending 00:57:31-01:03:31 while the ad container logs show requests at 01:02:47-01:03:17, and the payment span series is zero only in the window ending 00:57:31; the reason for these conflicting/zero spans is unknown and no traffic conclusion can be drawn for ad or payment.

Jaeger's sampled view is incomplete: the earliest frontend error-trace sample has data_as_of 00:54:59Z and traces_search_by_tags for 00:45-01:11 returned only traces up to that time, and a later query for 01:04:30-01:11:31 matched nothing, so no trace-level evidence is available for the second half of the error burst; error traces therefore cannot show whether ad/payment returned application errors later.

Trace span counts are not unique request counts and the metrics show increases only; the number of actual frontend requests that failed is unknown, and the ad span zero-windows may reflect a telemetry gap rather than email/absence of traffic.
next_steps: Inspect ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config change history (gitops/audit logs) and the flagd admin UI/API to timestamp when adFailure became 'on' and paymentFailure became '100%', and to confirm the currently effective values.
Check the audit/change record for the kubectl rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-18T00:53:51Z to identify the actor or automation that triggered it.

Compare ad and payment server-side gRPC metrics (rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket for rpc.grpc.status_code) around 00:54-01:04Z to determine whether the services returned application errors (as the adFailure/paymentFailure flags would produce) or no requests at all.
Re-check the frontend RequestErrorRate alert rule definition and current value in the system that fired it, since it is not present in this Prometheus rule set.
Collect frontend and flagd container logs (currently unavailable) around 00:53-01:05Z to see the exact client-side and flag-serving messages.
